\subsection{Broader comparison}
\label{sec:realworld-broad}
\emergencystretch=8em

This subsection adds the detector, citation, and gateway measurements from the local harness, and a hosted-model rerun recorded on the author's machine.

Lattice's OpenAI-compatible adapter called \path{https://openrouter.ai/api/v1}. The catalog check found 7 of the requested \texttt{:free} ids, and the listed prompt and completion prices were 0. Completed model rows: 7. Upstream HTTP 429 responses were retried. Pacing sleeps, that backoff, and the HTTP time of a failed attempt are excluded from Lattice time and from end-to-end time, so end-to-end time is Lattice processing plus the provider time of the attempt that returned. Provider time includes waiting for the response headers and reading the body. Completion tokens are capped at 8192. The adapter sends no temperature, \texttt{max\_tokens}, or reasoning field. A fetch wrapper adds temperature and the token cap to every request, and adds \texttt{reasoning.effort=low} for models whose catalog lists a reasoning parameter. A 400 that rejects that field is retried once without it. The Lattice rows therefore describe requests the adapter does not build on its own. Table~\ref{tab:rw-models} uses the provider string returned on the chat response. A drift cell is distinct successful answers, successful calls, and attempts. A RAG call succeeds when the run returns an answer that passes \texttt{mustCite}, which was called with \texttt{inline:~true} because the answers cite the clause inline. Output binding counts replayed receipts whose signed output hash matched the kept answer, over every replay row, including calls that kept an empty answer. The local row is the Ollama run in Section~\ref{sec:realworld} (drift n=3, overhead n=5). Hosted drift used n=10 when the call returned. This hosted recording is library commit \texttt{c5f79b0}, started at 2026-10-26 14:13 CDT (2026-10-26T19:13:36Z), on the author's machine. The local Ollama rows, the public-dataset rows, and the gateway rows are earlier recordings and are not from that machine. The plan called 5 short-prompt trials per model and replayed the RAG receipts (20 per model that returned them). Only free OpenRouter models were called. The single-agent stage and the image stage were left out of this recording. 
 On the local Ollama run, the median time outside the HTTP call was 2.4~ms (p95 15.0~ms, 0.439\% of that run's signed wall time). That localhost call returns the body with the headers, so the gap is processing time. Across hosted models with a successful signed short prompt, the median Lattice processing time was 1.66--3.03~ms, or 0.066--0.265\% of end-to-end time (1.7 to 3.0~ms and 0.07 to 0.27\% at the reported rounding). Table~\ref{tab:rw-lattice} gives the median and p95 in milliseconds and as a percentage. With five trials, p95 is the largest trial. The percentages are recomputed from the per-trial phase times as Lattice milliseconds over Lattice milliseconds plus the provider time of the attempt that returned. The \texttt{signedLatticePct} field stored in the previous \texttt{openrouter.json} also counts the HTTP time of retried attempts, so the comparison uses the recomputed rows for both runs. Lattice time includes \texttt{createAI()} construction and the fetch wrapper's JSON handling, so it is an upper bound. On the previous recording those medians were 1.10--1.69~ms, or 0.032--0.218\% of end-to-end time. The new medians are higher. Liquid's percentage p95 is 0.72\%, the highest hosted p95 in this run. The packed Lattice prompt added 62--81 prompt tokens at the median versus the one-line direct prompt. The paired provider-time difference on that longer prompt had medians from -1366 to 2300~ms. A negative value means the packed call returned sooner. The difference changes sign and is often larger than a short extra prefill can explain, because completion length, including reasoning tokens, moves the provider time by seconds. It is reported separately and is not added to Lattice processing time.

\path{thinkingmachines/inkling-small:free} is in the public catalog at price 0. Every measured call was rejected with HTTP 403 and the message that the model is only available on agentic harnesses, so this row has no latency sample.

Output binding in Table~\ref{tab:rw-models} counts whether the replayed output hash matched. The misses are \path{xingchen-agi/xing4.0-29b-a4b:free} 14/20; \path{nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free} 19/20; \path{liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free} 17/20. On every model that has a replay row, all 20 receipts verified, the offline replay materialized, and the altered copy was detected. The misses are the trials whose kept answer is empty after a provider error, HTTP 429, or an upstream timeout, so the string passed to \texttt{replayOffline} does not hash to the signed output. The run summary describes those misses as the free model giving a different answer on re-execution. They are not signature failures and not chain failures. \texttt{replayOffline} does not call the model; it checks the output the caller supplies.
These crews hit \texttt{crew-budget-exceeded} and are not successes. \path{liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free} used 1 iteration, kept 3 receipts, and the chain closed: yes, with 485~s of recorded slack. \path{poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free} used 2 iterations, kept 3 receipts, and the chain closed: yes, with 225~s of recorded slack. The harness allows 4 iterations and 180~s of wall time. The iteration counts are below that cap. The slack field holds pacing and HTTP 429 backoff that the Lattice processing clock excludes, and both slack totals are above 180~s. The likely cause is those free-tier waits exhausting the wall-clock budget. That reading is inferred from the timers, not from a log line that names the budget. The three-receipt chains still closed.
Crews that finished with a closed chain and parent kind success: \path{xingchen-agi/xing4.0-29b-a4b:free} (4 receipts); \path{nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free} (4 receipts); \path{nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free} (4 receipts); \path{dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free} (4 receipts).
These requested ids were absent from OpenRouter's catalog at rerun time, so they have no new row: \texttt{minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash:free}. \texttt{minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash:free} was measured in the previous recording.
The single-agent stage was not run. On the previous recording the single-agent return carried no receipt. That gap is open on this commit and was not rechecked, so this rerun does not show it fixed. The agent column is blank for that reason.
The image stage was not run. The color mismatch that follows is the earlier probe, at the previous recording, and was not rechecked on this commit. It remains an open gap.
On a 16$\times$16 solid red PNG, \path{nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free} answered red from a direct \texttt{image\_url} part: yes (answer red). The Lattice image artifact answered red: no (answer blue). The PNG bytes were present in the Lattice request body: yes. The direct response provider was Nvidia. This vision call set \texttt{reasoning.effort=none}.
The text arms use reasoning.effort=low. On this vision call, effort low and effort minimal each spent 8192 completion tokens on reasoning and returned empty content. This recorded call sets reasoning.effort=none. Lattice inlines the PNG in the text JSON. The direct arm sends an image\_url part.
Lattice's OpenAI-compatible request builder, which the openai, xai, openrouter, and lm-studio adapters share, sends each artifact as a text part holding JSON and never emits an image part. A data-URL string is inlined as text and binary bytes are dropped, so the model received no image part, and the Lattice arm answered blue for a red PNG.

Document-level precision, recall, and F1 use the harness overlap rule: a document is a true positive when any predicted span of that type overlaps a gold span. An undefined F1 means there were no positive predictions, or no gold documents and no false positives. spaCy \texttt{en\_core\_web\_sm} emits none of the four labels, so its precision and F1 are undefined and its recall is zero wherever a gold span exists. Figure~\ref{fig:rw-pii-f1} omits those undefined bars.

The rule is not symmetric across tools. For each type, Lattice contributes every occurrence of the one substring \texttt{detect()} returns, while the other tools contribute every span they emit. When Lattice's one match falls on a different number, the document is a false positive and a false negative for Lattice, while a multi-span tool can still score it from another span. GLiNER \citep{gliner} is the general \path{urchade/gliner_small-v2.1} model, not a PII fine-tune, and its processor truncated each document to 384 tokens, while LLM Guard \citep{llmguard} scanned 1,500-character windows with 200 characters of overlap. LLM Guard ran its default Anonymize scanner with recognizer \path{Isotonic/deberta-v3-base_finetuned_ai4privacy_v2}, which was fine-tuned on ai4privacy, so its ai4privacy scores can be optimistic. A single process was OOM-killed on long inputs, so each batch of 250 documents ran in its own process with a fresh Vault. Raw SSN labels are mapped when the NER map returns them unchanged. Presidio \citep{presidio} used its pattern and spaCy \citep{spacy} recognizers for its four in-scope entities, with \texttt{en\_core\_web\_sm} rather than its default \texttt{en\_core\_web\_lg}. Lattice is an in-process JavaScript regex and the other detectors are Python pipelines, so Figure~\ref{fig:rw-pii-latency} compares runtimes as well as detectors. The Lattice rows were measured with the detectors at commit \texttt{ae99fb5}.

On ASQA dev \citep{asqa} (n=948), a case-sensitive Wikipedia title substring matches 525 long answers and a case-insensitive substring matches 605. Square-bracket citations appear in 2 answers and overlap a gold title in 0. With \texttt{inline:~true}, \texttt{mustCite} accepts a gold title in 4. The structured default accepts a gold title in 0. These checks are different predicates. The structured default never reads the answer text.
 A local cross-encoder, \path{typeform/distilbert-base-uncased-mnli}, scored 696 of 948 pairs and labeled 296 entailed (empty 252, NEUTRAL 211, CONTRADICTION 189, ENTAILMENT 296). Median classification time was 820.0~ms. The premise is the gold knowledge text truncated to 1,800 characters and the hypothesis is the long answer. Pairs with an empty premise or answer were not scored. This is a support label, not a citation-string check.

LiteLLM \citep{litellm} here is an in-process client, not a proxy process. Its router sent eight short prompts to two identical Ollama deployments and returned 1 distinct route across 8 calls. That is a weak determinism check. The other wrappers are a LangChain callback handler \citep{langchain}, OpenLLMetry's in-process spans \citep{openllmetry}, and a local Portkey gateway \citep{portkey}. Helicone and Langfuse were not started.
 The latency rows are small samples (n=3--5 per arm). Each wrapper ran its calls in its own block, not interleaved with the direct arm, against \texttt{llama3.2:3b} on a CPU-only host. The min--max ranges overlap, so the p50 order reflects generation noise, not wrapper overhead.
